To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction of α-chlorovinyl sulfonamides with phosphorus nucleophiles is a new method for the synthesis of C,N-diphoshorylated N-(trichloroethyl)imines.

(i) C-Phosphorylated imines 1 react with O- and N-nucleophiles to give addition products 12, 13, 15, 16 and 19, which are functionalized derivatives of the α-aminophos- phonates, and with S-nucleophiles, such as mercaptoac-etic acid, to give novel C,N,S-triphosphorylated thia- zolidinones 18 and 20
the reaction of N-(trichloroethyl)imine 1 with triethyl phosphite or ethyl dipenyl phosphinite proceeds via the Perkow reaction to form C,N-diphosporated N-dichloroethylsulfonyl derivatives 8.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemistry of highly electrophilically activated imines, which are formed in the reaction of α-phosphorylsulfonyl chlorides 1 with O-, N- or S-nucleophiles.

the development of a new approach to highly electrophillic N-arylsulfonimines 1, which are readily accessible from the corresponding α-phosphorylsulfonamides, and with the investigation of their reactivity in various aza-Perkov reactions.

a new approach to the preparation of C-phosphoryl-substituted N-aryl-N-arylsulphonylimines 1 and their further transformations to C,N-diphosporanylated derivatives 8 and 9 and 2-phosphonylated thiazolidine derivatives 17, which are the functionalized analogues of the α-aminophosphate acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new C‐phosphorylated imines 1, 2a, 2b, 3, 4, 5, and 6 are highly electrophilically reactive compounds, and their reactions with nucleophiles are governed by the same rules as the reactions of the corresponding C‐unsubstituted imines.

the reaction of C-phosphoryl imines 1 with nucleophiles (O- and S-nucelophiles) proceeds in a regiospecific way, and that the reaction products are formed via addition of the nucleophile to C-Cl bond of the imine 1.
the C-phosphorylation of the N-arylsulfonimines is an important tool for the preparation of new types of electrophilic imines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C‐phosphorylated N-(trichloroethylidenesulfonamides) are highly electrophillic compounds and are able to react with nucleophiles.
we developed an efficient synthetic route to a new type of highly electrophillic N-sulphonylimines, which are readily available and can be easily modified by various nucleophiles.

the C-phosphorylation of the N-sulfonyl group of α-aminocarbanions 5, which is a very convenient and efficient method for the preparation of the previously unknown, highly reactive C- and C,N-diphos-phorylated N-(trichloroethyl)imines 1, is the key stage of the synthesis of a new type of highly electrophilically active N-arylsulfonimines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C-phosphoryl group is a powerful electron-withdrawing group, which can be exploited in the development of new synthetic strategies.

the use of amines in the aza‐Michael reaction is limited by the low nucleophilicity of the nitrogen lone pair, which can be significantly increased by the introduction of a phosphorus atom in the β‐position to nitrogen.
the use of C-Phosphorylated imines 1 in the aza‐Perkow reaction with trialkylphosphites or ethyl‐diphenylphosphinate leads to the formation of C,N‐diphosphorylated dichlorovinyl sulfonamides.
